focus: Accounting Precision, Founder Psychology, Financial Sovereignty, Tax Compliance SA

schedule.headline: The two ledgers in every business
schedule.body: There are two ledgers in every business: the one with numbers, and the one with the person behind them. Most advisors only ever open the first. This month, we're unpacking what it looks like to read both — the IQ of the balance sheet and the EQ of the founder holding it.

schedule.headline: Wealth. Health. Wellth.
schedule.body: Wealth. Health. Wellth. We merged the two words on purpose. A business can't be financially sound if the person running it is running on empty — and it can't be emotionally well if the numbers are a mess. That's the whole idea behind Integrated Wellth Solutions. More on this all month

schedule.headline: An accountant and a psychologist walk into a business review
schedule.body: An accountant and a psychologist walk into a business review. That's not a joke, that's our whole model. IQ + EQ. Numbers + nervous system.

schedule.headline: Why Marcia built Integrated Wellth Solutions
schedule.body: Marcia Kgaphola didn't set out to build 'just another accounting firm.' She kept seeing the same pattern in client meetings: the spreadsheet was fine, the founder wasn't. So she built Integrated Wellth Solutions around a simple belief — you can't separate a business owner's decisions from their state of mind. This month we're sharing more of that story.

schedule.headline: Three things nobody tells you when you start a business
schedule.body: Video concept: Talking-head hook — 'Three things nobody tells you when you start a business...' cut to on-screen text listing: 1) the money stuff is emotional 2) you'll make decisions from fear more than logic 3) your business grows exactly as far as your nervous system lets it. End card: 'This is why we exist.'

schedule.headline: Accounting precision + founder psychology
schedule.body: "I got tired of watching brilliant business owners make excellent decisions on paper and terrible ones under pressure." — that tension is the reason Integrated Wellth Solutions exists: accounting precision, paired with the psychology of the person making the call.

schedule.headline: What does 'financial sovereignty' actually mean?
schedule.body: What does 'financial sovereignty' actually mean? It's not about being rich. It's about a business that can run, make decisions, and survive a bad month without everything depending on one exhausted founder. That's the outcome we build toward. Save this for the days you need reminding.

schedule.headline: The true test of financial sovereignty
schedule.body: Financial sovereignty isn't a bigger bank balance. It's a business that doesn't collapse the week you take a holiday.

schedule.headline: The two-week test
schedule.body: Quick question for the business owners in the room: if you took two weeks off right now, with no laptop, would your business still be standing when you got back? That question — not your bank balance — is the real test of financial sovereignty. Something we think about a lot.

schedule.headline: When your business is thriving but you haven't slept
schedule.body: Video concept: POV text-on-screen — 'When your business is thriving but you haven't slept properly in a month' — voiceover talks through founder burnout signs (decision fatigue, guilt about resting, checking the bank app at 2am). Ends on: 'The books can be healthy and you can not be. We look at both.'

schedule.headline: Founder burnout reality
schedule.body: Founder burnout rarely shows up as burnout. It shows up as snapping at your team, avoiding your bookkeeping, or saying yes to every client because saying no feels unsafe. The psychology of running a business is inseparable from the numbers it produces.

schedule.headline: Exhaustion isn't a personal failing
schedule.body: Real talk: the exhaustion isn't a personal failing. It's what happens when a business is built entirely around one person's capacity. Tag a founder who needs to hear this today.
